brief: UBS's weekly derivatives note argues three capitulation signals have been triggered together: Excess Flow of -$365bn (largest on record), UBS RMM retail flow buying the dip at the 68th percentile vs. 3 years after the largest selling episode since Covid, and a VIX Cross-Asset Rank of 96%, meaning equity volatility is extremely elevated versus other asset classes. Together these imply forced selling and oversold conditions, so UBS expects SPX to establish a low Monday as systematic selling and hedge-fund unwind pressure fade. Three systematic strategies sold an estimated $170-210bn today (Risk Control $95-125bn, Leveraged ETFs $50-55bn, CTA $25-30bn), and UBS expects Risk Control to sell another $200-270bn over the next two days before both Risk Control and CTA flows shrink sharply after Monday. UBS Prime Brokerage long/short net leverage sits at the 18th percentile vs. 1 year and the long/short ratio at the 8th percentile, so net long exposure is already very low and short-squeeze risk is elevated. Investor conversations were not panicked, with many clients waiting to buy further weakness rather than capitulating broadly. A fourth test, the VIX/SPX intraday high-low ratio, was not met since SPX is only -5.9% from its peak versus the roughly -9.5% usually needed.
